subject: ventures/charity-bunching-planner
professional: a CPA or EA doing year-end charitable planning for households near the standard deduction; first checks: the 2026 constants and OBBBA charitable rules (0.5%-of-AGI floor for itemizers, 1,000/2,000 non-itemizer cash deduction that excludes DAFs and is not indexed, 60% cash / 30% appreciated-stock AGI limits, 35% cap on itemized benefit in the 37% bracket), whether the saving is a bracket-based tax difference or a flat-rate shortcut, and whether 'tax saved' is measured against a no-gift baseline

evidence.correctness: Recomputed by hand from 2026 law (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 MFJ standard deduction 32,200 and brackets 24,800/100,800/211,400/403,550; IRC 170(b)(1)(I) 0.5% floor and 170(p) 2,000 MFJ non-itemizer cash deduction as added by OBBBA, P.L. 119-21; from the auditor's knowledge, irs.gov not fetched) with `node /tmp/cbp-audit/hand.mjs` and `node /tmp/cbp-audit/brackets.mjs`. Case A (AGI 200k, other 20k, gift 10k, 2 years, 22%): direct 2x(2,000x0.22)=880; bunch year 1 deposits 18,000, 20,000+18,000-1,000-32,200=4,800 x0.22=1,056, plus 440 -> 1,496, gain 616: tool matches to the cent, and the real-bracket return agrees (all in the 22% band). The tool's chosen years also match a real-bracket re-ranking of every allowed schedule in two 6- and 8-year cases (years 1,4 and 1,5). Not a 3: (1) when other itemized deductions exceed the standard deduction the 'tax saved' headline counts deductions unrelated to giving (other 60k, one year, gift 8k: tool says 12,987 saved by giving directly; the gift causes (8,000-900)x0.37=2,627, 4.9x overstated, calc.mjs:69, index.html:134); (2) the dollar figures use one flat rate, so a bunched deduction that drops through a bracket is overstated: AGI 140k, 3-year bunch of 41,000, tool gain 5,676 vs 3,566 from the MFJ bracket table (59% high) and 11,352 vs 7,132 over 6 years; disclosed on the page; (3) the shipped example pairs a 32% federal rate with AGI 180k and a 32,000 (MFJ-sized) standard deduction, whose real 2026 MFJ marginal rate is 22%; the example gain 9,253 is 6,752 at 22%+5%.
evidence.completeness: Every claimed feature runs end to end through analyze(): exhaustive schedule search up to 15 years under a gap limit (15 years, 0.14 s), direct-every-year baseline, every-k-years cycles with best offset, 0.5% floor, 60% ceiling with a warning above it, non-itemizer cash cap with DAF excluded, inflation of deductions/AGI, DAF growth reported as money left, appreciated-stock gain avoided, CSV export, opt-out local usage counter. No stubs or TODOs. Served copy clean (`node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs charity-bunching-planner`: no placeholder or retired origin). Small gaps: the years label says '2 to 15' but 1 is accepted; the README's own 'path to revenue' items (bracket mode, stock limits, carryforward, preparer printout) are listed as not built, honestly.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/charity-bunching-planner && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 30 tests, 30 pass, ~230 ms. Tests pin yearSaving with hand numbers (floor, cap, ceiling), deposit sizing, search vs an enumeration, and page invariants. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: covered-year direct gift -> 0 caught; stock saving without the stock share caught; tail-gap rule <= maxGap -> <= maxGap+1 SURVIVED; standard deduction no longer inflated SURVIVED; 60%-AGI warning threshold 0.6 -> 0.7 SURVIVED; itemized flag >= -> > survived (near-equivalent, display only). No test runs a multi-year case with a hand-checked total, and none exercises inflation.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (215 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Pure functions, no dependencies, output escaped, storage access guarded, exhaustive search small enough to be exact. Defects: blank or unparsable fields silently become the example values (index.html:121), so clearing 'Other itemized deductions' computes on 22,000 and analyze()'s missing-input warnings are unreachable from a blank field; `first = mask.indexOf(true)` recomputed inside the year loop (calc.mjs:97, harmless); comments call the 170(p) deduction 'above-the-line' though it is taken in computing taxable income, not AGI (calc.mjs:12).
evidence.claims: Backed: 'searches every schedule' (calc.mjs:145, exhaustive, exact for the model), floor/ceiling/non-itemizer rules (checked above), DAF excluded from the non-itemizer deduction, growth not counted as saving, 'Not decided' list names the flat rate, AMT, the high-earner cap, the stock AGI limit, carryforward, state rules and irrevocability; disclaimer on page, README and llms.txt; privacy line matches usage.mjs (local storage, DNT/GPC honoured, opt-out); served origins clean. Not backed: README:22 'verified against an independent brute force' (the test enumerates masks but scores them with the same evaluate(), so it checks the search loop, not the arithmetic); the verdict's 'saves $X in tax' is relative to the standard deduction, not to not giving, which misstates the figure for itemizers (see correctness).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a preparer with an MFJ client near the standard deduction types gift, other itemized, AGI, rate and the 2,000 cap and gets the deposit years, per-year deposit/direct/grant table, cycle comparison and a CSV; the years chosen held up under a real-bracket re-ranking in the cases tried, so the timing answer is usable. Hit in the first hour: the dollar saving needs brackets (the client's bunch year usually crosses one); no filing-status selector or constants, so the user must know the 2026 figures; a 37% client gets the 2/37 benefit haircut ignored; stock-funded deposits are held to the 60% cash limit instead of 30% (the 60% warning does not fire between 30% and 60%); no carryforward valuation; the 'tax saved' total misleads for a client who already itemizes.
evidence.domain: Matches the 2026 rules where it models them: 0.5%-of-AGI floor applied only when itemizing, 170(p) non-itemizer deduction kept flat (not indexed) and denied for DAF deposits, cash gifts to a DAF sponsor at the 60% limit, 'give min(gift, cap) directly in off years' is the right post-OBBBA tactic. Departures from how a CPA would run it: flat marginal rate instead of a with/without tax computation; OBBBA 35% cap on itemized benefit (37% bracket) not modelled; 30% AGI limit for appreciated stock to a DAF not applied; the floor/ceiling ordering above 60% and the carryforward are only warned about; a state rate is simply added to the federal rate and applied to the federal deduction difference.

defects.what: 'Tax saved' is measured against the standard deduction, not against not giving: when other itemized deductions exceed the standard deduction the headline counts them as saving from giving (60k other, 8k gift: 12,987 shown vs 2,627 caused by the gift). The gain is still right.

One flat marginal rate: a bunched deduction that crosses a bracket overstates the dollar saving (59% in a 3-year MFJ case at AGI 140k). Disclosed on the page, but the only fix a preparer would accept is a bracket mode.

The shipped example combines a 32% federal rate with AGI 180k and an MFJ-sized 32,000 standard deduction; the real 2026 MFJ marginal rate there is 22%, so the example overstates the gain (9,253 vs 6,752). The standard deduction default 32,000 is neither the 2026 32,200 nor the 2025 31,500.
Blank or unparsable fields silently become the example values (clearing 'Other itemized' computes on 22,000), so the missing-input warnings never fire from a blank field.

Stock-funded deposits are held to the 60% cash limit; the 30% limit for appreciated stock to a DAF is not applied and the 60% warning does not fire between 30% and 60% of AGI. Disclosed in 'Not decided'. The OBBBA 35% cap on itemized benefit for the 37% bracket is likewise only disclosed.
Seeded changes to the tail-gap rule, the inflation of the standard deduction and the 60%-AGI warning threshold all left every test green; no multi-year case has a hand-checked total.
README says the optimum is verified against an 'independent brute force', but the test scores both sides with the same evaluate().
Years label says '2 to 15' but 1 is accepted without a warning.
Comments call the 170(p) non-itemizer deduction 'above-the-line'; it is taken in computing taxable income, not AGI (no effect on the numbers, since the floor uses AGI).

verdict: A clean, honest bunching solver whose arithmetic is exact for its stated model (a 2-year case recomputed by hand from the 2026 tables matches to the cent, and its chosen deposit years survived a real-bracket re-ranking), with the post-OBBBA rules a CPA checks first modelled correctly: 0.5% floor for itemizers only, the non-indexed 2,000 non-itemizer cash deduction that excludes DAFs, and the 60% cash ceiling. It misses the bar on correctness and verification: the 'tax saved' headline is measured against the standard deduction rather than against not giving (4.9x overstated for an itemizer), the flat rate overstates bracket-crossing savings (59% in a common case, disclosed), the shipped example pairs a 32% rate with a 22%-bracket household, and four of six seeded mutants (one near-equivalent) survived. Finished for what it claims; not yet a preparer-grade dollar figure.
